standard.title: Reflect on target language and English structures using metalanguage
standard.description: reflect on similarities and differences between target language and English language structures and features, using metalanguage
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can compare target language and English structures using metalanguage across grammatical features, text types and persuasive language (AC9LS6U03). They have not yet used metalanguage to analyse whole-text coherence, or explored historical vocabulary influences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on similarities and differences between target language and English language structures using metalanguage — including whole-text coherence, text-type conventions, vocabulary patterns and historical influences.

nodes.label: Whole-text coherence and text-type conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use metalanguage to compare whole-text coherence features and text-type conventions across the target language and English.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two whole-text coherence features in a target language text using metalanguage; compare at least one text-type convention across the target language and English.
nodes.typical_width: Compare descriptive, reflective and persuasive language across text types in both languages; identify and analyse language features used to create effects in different text types; compare textual coherence elements — cohesive devices, introductions, summaries, linked paragraphs; compare text conventions across communication modes.
wider: Analyse a target language and English text of the same type — use metalanguage to annotate every coherence feature and compare how each language achieves coherence
Compare advertising texts in the target language and English — annotate every persuasive feature in each and compare how each language constructs persuasion
nodes.hinge_reason: Whole-text metalinguistic analysis is the analytical tool for the text evaluation and synthesis work at subsequent bands. Students who only apply metalanguage at word or sentence level cannot engage with text-level evaluation.

response_modes.reason: Whole-text coherence analysis requires students to hold the full text in view while applying metalanguage to structural and connective features. Structured annotation tasks scaffold this whole-text analytical attention.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two whole-text coherence features in a target language text using metalanguage
Compares at least one text-type convention across the target language and English, explaining the difference

nodes.label: Vocabulary patterns and historical influences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collect and analyse target language-English vocabulary patterns and explain how historical and cultural contact has shaped target language vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three vocabulary pairs using a systematic cross-language pattern; identify at least one historical vocabulary influence on the target language.
nodes.typical_width: Collect vocabulary pairs across systematic pattern categories; recognise systematic cross-language vocabulary patterns; identify vocabulary borrowed through historical cultural contact; explore how political, historical and social changes have introduced vocabulary into the target language.
wider: Research a historical period of cultural contact that influenced the target language — find examples of loanwords and explain what the borrowing reveals about that historical relationship
Create a visual etymology map tracing historical influences on target language vocabulary — with examples of each influence

response_modes.reason: Vocabulary history and pattern awareness develops through encountering varied examples across different historical influences and language families.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Tracing target language vocabulary history connects language learning to genuine historical and cultural understanding — students engaging with etymology are engaging with the history of the communities that speak the language.
success_criteria: Identifies at least three target language-English vocabulary pairs using a systematic pattern
Identifies at least one historical vocabulary influence on the target language and explains the historical context
